title: Light That Is Not Even: Local Thresholds and the Integral Image

questions.question: A bench lamp lights the left of a frame dimly and the right brightly. Why can no single threshold separate dark marks from the background?
options: A mark on the bright side is lighter than plain background on the dim side: one threshold found 0.582 of the marks and marked 0.446 of everything else
questions.explanation: The question per pixel is whether it is darker than its neighbours.

questions.question: What makes the sum of any rectangle cost four reads?
options: A summed area table: entry (x, y) is the sum of everything above and to the left, so a box is four entries added and subtracted
questions.explanation: The table is built once in one pass.

questions.question: A box centred at the corner sticks out of the picture. What should its mean divide by?
options: The count of pixels actually inside the picture: 81 of the 17 by 17 box, giving 90.0 on a flat picture of 90
questions.explanation: Dividing by the whole box lowers the mean towards the border, so marks there are missed.

questions.question: What happens when the window is smaller than a mark?
options: The window averages the mark with itself and sees nothing odd: a radius of 1 found only 0.317 of the marks
questions.explanation: The window must be bigger than the mark.

questions.question: What happens when the window is as wide as the picture?
options: It is a global threshold again: radius 100 found 0.577 and marked 0.405, nearly the same as one Otsu threshold
questions.explanation: Between the two, 8 to 16 here, it works.

questions.question: What does the offset do on a noisy picture?
options: Asks a pixel to be darker than the mean by a margin, so noise is not marked: with noise of 6 levels, 0 marked 0.269 of the background and 20 marked 0.001 while finding 0.987
questions.explanation: Choose it below the marks' contrast and above the noise.
